Package org.apache.juneau.rest.server

Annotation Interface Child

@Target({}) @Retention(RUNTIME) public @interface Child
Host-side setting seed for the @Rest(childrenDefs=...) attribute.

Declares a routed child class and lets the host seed a curated set of @Rest-level settings onto that child's otherwise-isolated RestContext — the child-resource analog of @Rest(mixinDefs=...). This is the host-side complement to @Rest(children=...) (which takes bare classes and offers no seed hook).

Example:

@Rest( childrenDefs=@Child(type=FooChild.class, callLogger=SeedLogger.class) ) public class MyResource { ... }

Seed semantics

Unlike @Mixin overrides (which win over an inherited chain), children are isolated from the host's resolution chain by design, so a @Child seed doesn't override anything — it seeds settings onto an otherwise-isolated child context:

  • Additive-security (guards, converters, roleGuard, rolesDeclared) — the host contributes, the child can't remove or weaken it (list-shaped members prepend; the two role-based members AND-stack alongside the child's own value).
  • Child-wins scalars (callLogger, partSerializer, partParser, debug, defaultCharset, maxInput) — the seed is a default/fallback; the child's own explicit @Rest declaration wins when present.

A child's own @Rest(noInherit="&lt;property&gt;") cuts the corresponding @Child seed too, for both buckets above — the child always stays in full control of its own configuration.

There is no noInherit() member on @Child itself (nothing to cut in an isolated context), and no path()/paths() re-mount member (the child's own @Rest(path) stays authoritative).
